subject: Hosted API usage runway + peak spike clarification
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@clearbridge.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex R. <alex@clearbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap from today's hosted API pricing call

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good overview and helpful nuance on batching/kv caching. Per our internal convo, I wanted to capture the traffic profile we discussed so you can confirm hosted pricing fit / vs Reserved. High-level summary: 

- Current pilot: ~3.2M tokens/month (low-touch chat flows)
- 90-day ramp target: 30M - 80M tokens/month (conservative / aggressive scenarios)
- 6–12 month target (if UX tests go well): 80M - 240M tokens/month
- Typical request payloads: average ~450 tokens in, ~500 tokens out (so ~950 tokens/request); some document-summarization paths are ~2.5k tokens
- Baseline concurrent steady-state: ~30-60 TPS depending on region; daytime peak windows we expect frequent ~120 TPS; occasional burst events up to ~650 TPS for short 1–5 minute spikes during product launches
- Budget: internal stakeholders are aiming for a predictable $/1M target — ballpark $8–15 per 1M tokens depending on SLAs and burst handling

Attached: clearbridge-traffic-sample.csv — a week snapshot. Can you confirm whether hosted API at Redwood would accommodate the 650 TPS bursts without a Dedicated commitment, and what the expected unit pricing would look like at the 80M and 240M bands? Also useful: a simple estimate of monthly cost at $/1M price points so procurement can see three scenarios (conservative / base / expansion).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Platform
ClearBridge AI

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@clearbridge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's hosted API pricing call

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 09:18 AM Nina Patel <nina.patel@clearbridge.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo this morning — good overview and helpful nuance on batching/kv caching. Per our internal convo, I wanted to capture the traffic profile we discussed so you can confirm hosted pricing fit / vs Reserved.

Great summary, Nina — this is exactly the detail we need. Short answers up front: hosted API can support your steady-state and short bursts, but there are tradeoffs at the 240M/mo level where Reserved (Dedicated) typically becomes more cost-effective and gives predictable peak TPS guarantees. Below I outline our initial assumptions and a quick ballpark estimate so procurement can start modelling.

Assumptions used (please confirm):
- Avg tokens/request used for estimate: 950 tokens (you noted ~950 average)
- Month = 30 days, 24/7 distribution with peak windows concentrated 10–16 PST
- Burst handling: hosted API allows bursts via autoscaling and regional fallback, but sustained 600+ TPS for >5 minutes may incur throttling or higher transient latencies unless you commit to a reserved pool.

Ballpark hosted pricing (illustrative; final quote will follow):
- 80M tokens/mo: $12 / 1M => ~$960/month
- 160M tokens/mo: $11 / 1M => ~$1,760/month
- 240M tokens/mo: $10 / 1M => ~$2,400/month

Notes on unit economics and SLA: these price points assume standard hosted SLA and best-effort burst support. If you require guaranteed 650 TPS bursts (SLO for response < 350ms p95 during bursts), we recommend Redwood Dedicated with an estimated committed monthly spend that I can model separately.

Next asks from our side to firm numbers: 
1) Can you confirm the 95th-percentile requests/minute during your peak window (we need a 1-hour and 1-day view)
2) Typical token distribution (percent of calls under 1k tokens, 1k-2.5k, >2.5k) — the sample CSV helps but we may need a 7–14 day sample
3) Procurement constraints: is there a hard $/1M cap you cannot exceed?

I've attached a quick calc (calc_estimate.xlsx) showing the above scenarios and the math so procurement can tweak assumptions. If useful I can also run a short stress test from our hosted sandbox to validate burst handling — would you like that?

I'll loop in Jordan and Karthik for capacity modelling and to decide whether to propose a dedicated recommendation.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@clearbridge.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex R. <alex@clearbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's hosted API pricing call

Thanks — that helps. Quick clarifications inline: 
- 95th-percentile for a high-volume marketing window last quarter hit ~380 TPS sustained for 12 minutes; typical weekday peak ~110–130 TPS sustained for 2–3 hours;
- Token distribution (roughly): 72% under 1k, 22% 1k–2.5k, 6% >2.5k;
- Procurement: target ceiling is $12 / 1M but can stretch to $14/1M if we get explicit burst guarantees and a 99.9% uptime SLA

I attached a snapshot of the busiest week (traffic-week-snapshot.png). Yes please run a 30-minute stress test from the sandbox aimed at 500 TPS with the same token-size mix and share telemetry — that will help our infra folks sign off. If the stress test looks good, procurement wants a short one-page pricing comparison (hosted vs Dedicated) we can circulate internally.

Nina

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@clearbridge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's hosted API pricing call — next steps and asks

Thanks for the clarifications, Nina — very helpful. Agreed next steps below and owners: 

1) Sandbox stress test (Evelyn / Jordan): schedule 30-min test targeting 500 TPS with token mix you provided. Deliverable: telemetry dashboard link + latency & error rate summary. Target date: Nov 18 PST.
2) Hosted vs Dedicated one-pager (Evelyn): I'll prepare a concise comparison including: price ladder we discussed, burst behavior, average p95 latency expectations during steady and burst, and an example commitment math for a Dedicated pool. Deliverable: one-page PDF for procurement by Nov 19.
3) Additional telemetry sample (Nina): please share a 14-day request log (anonymized) or allow temporary S3 upload for our infra team to ingest — we will treat it as PII-free and delete after modeling.
4) Procurement constraints (Nina/procurement): confirm final $/1M ceiling; you indicated $12 preferred ceiling, $14 stretch with guarantees. If that holds we'll prepare options at both levels.

Quick ballpark recap using your 80M/mo scenario at 950 tokens/request (for procurement modelling): 
- Estimated requests/month: ~84k (80M / 950)
- Baseline hosted cost at $12 / 1M: ~$960/month
- Baseline hosted cost at $14 / 1M: ~$1,120/month

I'll attach the one-pager and the stress test invite once times are locked. I'm putting the HubSpot deal link in this thread for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4897

If you prefer a short synchronous 20-minute call after the stress test to review telemetry, I'm happy to schedule.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
https://calendly.com/redwood-evelyn/30min
